common_name: Bowe Derek Hosta (Purple-Petioled Yellow Hosta from David Bowe)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; give it enough morning light to bring out the full yellow leaf color without scorching.

directions: Bowe Derek is a recent introduction from hybridizer David Bowe, offered through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. Rich yellow leaves are set off by dark purple petioles and scapes in the style of 'One Man's Treasure', with purple-striped flowers adding further contrast. Grow in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade with some morning sun to bring out full yellow color without leaf scorch. Divide congested clumps in early spring once the clump has bulked up over several seasons.

common_name: Even Better Hosta (Shiny Yellow Sport of Twice as Nice)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; some morning sun helps keep the yellow leaf color bright.

directions: Even Better is a bright yellow sport of the fragrant-flowered 'Twice as Nice', introduced by Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. Its glossy, shiny leaves and vigorous growth habit set it apart from its parent, and like 'Twice as Nice' it bears fragrant flowers in summer. Grow in partial shade with some morning sun to keep the yellow coloring bright, in moist, well-drained soil. Divide clumps every few years in spring as they become congested.

common_name: Notice Me Hosta (Faded Teal Leaves with Creamy Margins)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; deeper shade helps preserve the blue-teal leaf color through summer.

directions: Notice Me is a new hosta from hybridizer Doug Beilstein, introduced through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. Its soft, faded teal-blue leaves are edged in creamy margins, an unusual color combination that the nursery notes holds its blue cast well into late summer. Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, humus-rich soil, since strong sun fades the blue leaf color faster. Divide established clumps in early spring as new growth emerges.

common_name: Christine's Joy Hosta (Shiny Dark Green Mini-Mounding Sport of Tiki Bar)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; small hostas like this one establish well in containers or bed edges.

directions: Christine's Joy is a shiny, dark green sport of 'Tiki Bar' (itself a sport of 'Appletini'), introduced by Joe Parisi through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery and named in memory of Parisi's late wife Chris. It forms a tight, small, flat mound similar to its parent, making it well suited to edging or container display. Grow in shade to partial shade in evenly moist, well-drained soil. Divide small clumps carefully in spring, since miniature and small hostas take longer to rebuild size after division.

common_name: Forest Nymph Hosta (Ruffled Small Hosta with Yellow-to-Cream Margins)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with some morning sun to bring out the spring margin color.

directions: Forest Nymph is a new small, ruffled hosta from originator Randy Goodwin, introduced through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. Light green leaves are edged in yellow in spring, shifting to a creamy white margin by summer, and the clump spreads quickly into an airy, whirling mound. It suits mass plantings or containers in partial shade with some morning sun, in moist, humus-rich soil. Divide every few years as the clump fills in.

common_name: Our Mouse Hosta (Olive-Centered Mouse Ears Sport)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; true miniatures establish best in rock gardens, troughs, or small bed edges.

directions: Our Mouse is a sport discovered in hybridizer Doug Beilstein's garden, introduced through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. It resembles the popular 'Holy Mouse Ears' when it first emerges, but its leaf center stays olive-green through the season rather than turning white, and like other hostas in the 'Mouse Ears' group it can occasionally revert to the solid coloring of 'Blue Mouse Ears'. Grow in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil, as befits a true miniature. Divide sparingly, since miniature hostas are slow to recover size after division.

common_name: First Blush Hosta (Green Leaves Blushing Purplish Red, Patented)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with some morning sun to intensify red coloring.

directions: First Blush (U.S. Plant Patent 28,920) is bred and promoted by Bob Solberg at Green Hill Farm nursery as the nursery's first red-leafed hosta introduction. Green leaves emerge with red petioles and red margins, and the color blushes further into a purplish red across the whole leaf as the season progresses. Grow in partial shade with some morning sun to intensify the red coloring, in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil. Established clumps can be divided in early spring once they have filled in.

common_name: Flash Freeze Hosta (Powder Blue Cupped and Puckered Large Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade to preserve the powder-blue leaf color.

directions: Flash Freeze is a new introduction from hybridizer Doug Beilstein, offered through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. Its powder-blue leaves are cupped and somewhat puckered, with a tendency to overlap and wrap around their own petioles for a distinctive, layered look. Grow in shade to partial shade in moist, humus-rich soil to preserve the blue leaf color through the season. Divide large clumps in early spring as new shoots emerge.

common_name: Avocado Toast Hosta (Dark Green-Centered Sport of Lemon Snap)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, siting it where the red petioles can be seen up close.

directions: Avocado Toast is a sport of the red-petioled 'Lemon Snap', introduced through Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm nursery. It keeps its parent's red petioles and puckered, cupped leaf form while adding a distinctive dark green leaf center that contrasts with the lighter surrounding leaf. Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil. Divide congested clumps in early spring.

common_name: Cherry Cheesecake Hosta (Yellow Hosta with Bright Red Petioles and Scapes)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with some morning sun to bring out strong yellow leaf color and red petiole contrast.

directions: Cherry Cheesecake is a yellow, upright hosta bred by Bob Solberg at Green Hill Farm nursery as a sibling to 'Ruby Earrings'. Bright red petioles, bracts, and scapes stand out above the upright yellow foliage, with red coloring visible well up into the leaf itself. Grow in partial shade with some morning sun for strong yellow color and good red contrast, in moist, humus-rich soil. It grows taller than 'Ruby Earrings' and benefits from division every few years as the clump matures.
